Full regression: 56/56 pytest cases pass (48 pre-existing + 8 new). Frontend testing skipped per spec (backend-only fix). No modifications to /app/backend/watcher.py or wallet.py or server.py.
critical_code_review_comments: watcher._scan_chain_once fetches ALL users every poll (currently 77) — with 4 chains and Alchemy free-tier limits this is guaranteed to trip 429s continuously. Because the new strict cursor-hold policy (rate_limited==0) is now the gate, the cursor may NEVER advance in production until you switch to the batched alchemy_getAssetTransfers with toAddresses[] (docstring already flags this at N>1k, but with 4 chains you're effectively there at N=77). Recommend: batch toAddress in groups of 50 per RPC call, OR add exponential backoff + per-user retry queue so a single pathological user cannot indefinitely block the chain cursor. Otherwise a stuck user_29-style tail permanently freezes the whole chain scan window.

The strict cursor-hold makes correctness dependent on all users being scanned in one poll cycle — if the process is restarted mid-poll, the cursor holds and everything is re-scanned (good) but there is no metric/alert on 'chain X has not advanced its cursor in N minutes' — recommend a lightweight probe / dashboard field.

WATCHER_INITIAL_LOOKBACK_<CHAIN> only picks up positive digit strings via isdigit() — negative or hex values silently fall back to the default. Not a bug per se, but worth a debug log when the env is present but ignored.

watcher.py still keeps 'from wallet import _derive_by_kind' as a function-local import inside _scan_chain_once — original circular-avoidance reason no longer applies since wallet.py doesn't import watcher. Cleanup opportunity.

The strict rate_limited==0 cursor-hold means live watcher logs will keep showing 'watcher [X] rate-limited on N/63 users this poll' — this is EXPECTED behaviour and cursors WILL be stuck in prod until the batched-toAddresses refactor lands.
rca of the issue: Two coupled bugs caused the missing BNB deposit for user_29 (thirdeyeion): (a) INITIAL_LOOKBACK_BLOCKS=300 was ~15 min of BNB history — when the BNB chain was enabled AFTER the deposit hit, the fresh cursor started forward of the deposit's block; (b) the cursor-advance policy 'advance if <33% of users were rate-limited' meant a consistently-rate-limited user (user_29 always in the 429 bucket) had their scan window silently skipped every poll. Fix in watcher.py: default lookback raised to 7200 blocks (~1 day ETH / ~6h BNB) with per-chain env override WATCHER_INITIAL_LOOKBACK_<CHAIN>; cursor now only advances when rate_limited==0. Reproduced by monkeypatching AlchemyRPC.asset_transfers to raise HTTPStatusError(429) for one derived EVM address across a 3-user seed set and asserting the system.<chain>_last_block cursor stayed pinned at 1000; then removing the 429 patch and asserting the cursor advanced to head-CONFIRMATIONS. Mitigation for the caller of this bug: batch toAddresses in a single RPC to reduce 429 pressure so the strict cursor-hold policy stays unblocked at scale.
